title_ru: Осирис — Mendes 1902: золотой фаллический футляр и разрыв provenance
title_en: Osiris — Mendes 1902 gold phallus sheath control and provenance fracture

primary_breakthrough.source: J. E. Quibell, Note on a Tomb Found at Tell er Roba, ASAE 3 (1902), 245-249
primary_breakthrough.finding: The primary excavation report for the 1902 Nesbanebdjedet burial at Mendes documents gold foil used as rough sheaths for fingers, toes, and the phallus of the deceased.
primary_breakthrough.importance: The exact conjunction MENDES + GOLD + PHALLUS + FUNERARY BODY-PART EQUIPMENT is now primary-source documented rather than hypothetical.

provenance_breakthrough.finding: The 1902 discovery was disturbed before official control: workmen removed hundreds of shabtis and unknown additional objects; Quibell indicates some gold elements were likely taken, and an official annual-report summary states that some Mendes gold objects were stolen before inspector Aly Habib secured the find for the Museum.
provenance_breakthrough.research_effect: Reconstruct the original assemblage through excavation records, old catalogues, museum inventories, correspondence and institutional provenance. Do not pursue antiquities through the market or onsite searching.
provenance_breakthrough.not_established: No missing/stolen object is identified as an Osiris relic, and the identity of the missing gold subset is unresolved.

CAIRO_CG_53465_53469.known: The Met points to these five Cairo Catalogue Général numbers; they belong to Georges Vernier's 1927 Bijoux et orfèvreries fascicle covering CG 53172-53855.
CAIRO_CG_53465_53469.unknown: Exact CG-number-to-Quibell-object mapping remains unresolved from publicly indexed material.
CAIRO_CG_53465_53469.next: Retrieve Vernier pages/object cards and map all five numbers to surviving gold equipment.

official_nodes: Leiden lead via British Museum bibliography
Frank H. McClung Museum lead via British Museum curator note
DISPERSED_SISTER_OBJECTS.warning: Homonymous Nesbanebdjedet individuals must be separated by mother name, titles, inscriptions, dimensions and excavation provenance.

BM_TELL_EL_RUBA_15.result: The place-index set is dominated by ordinary shabtis and a small number of figures; no sealed/nested/reliquary or internal-anomaly hit surfaced in the first pass.

XRAY_CT_CONSERVATION.meaning: No publicly indexed X-ray/CT result specific to the 1902 Mendes gold assemblage was found. This is not evidence that institutional imaging does not exist.
XRAY_CT_CONSERVATION.next: Egyptian Museum Cairo conservation/radiography records for CG 53465-53469 become the highest imaging target.

causal_graph_update.after: MENDES 1902 -> NESBANEB-DJEDET BURIAL -> DOCUMENTED GOLD BODY-PART KIT -> DOCUMENTED GOLD PHALLUS SHEATH -> INCOMPLETE PROVENANCE -> CAIRO CG 53465-53469 / MISSING GOLD TRACE
causal_graph_update.interpretation: The search has moved from speculative material/form matching to a documented physical analogue and an archival provenance break. The analogue is not the divine relic.

next_gate.goal: Resolve the exact museum identity and survival status of the documented 1902 gold phallus sheath and all four companion CG entries, then check conservation/imaging records.
next_gate.stop_condition: Do not promote any object to OSIRIS_RELIC_CANDIDATE without independent Osirian relic linkage beyond Mendes provenance, gold, or phallic function.
